candidates.issues: Uses the imperative form which is acceptable but less common than present tense plural in modern Hebrew recipes. Translates 'peaks' literally to 'פסגות' instead of the more idiomatic 'קצף'.
Uses standard present tense plural verbs, which is great. However, it translates vanilla 'seeds' to 'זרעים' (instead of the standard 'גרגירים') and 'peaks' to 'פסגות' (instead of 'קצף').
Leaves the English word 'pasta' instead of translating 'paste' to 'מחית'. Unnecessarily includes literal English translations in parentheses like '(שמנת כפולה)'.
Uses the imperative form (less common but acceptable). Like A and B, it translates 'peaks' literally to 'פסגות' instead of 'קצף'.
